note: Same spelling as été, past participle of être ("been"). en été = in summer.
Vulgar; very common in speech. Also an adjective: c'est con = that's stupid.
ex: Quel con ! — What an idiot!
Le départ est à huit heures. — Departure is at eight.

note: être au courant = to be aware/informed; courant d'air = draught.
ex: Tu es au courant ? — Have you heard?

note: au moyen de = by means of; les moyens = (financial) means. Also adj: average.
ex: Il n'y a pas d'autre moyen. — There's no other way.
Au contraire ! — On the contrary!
J'ai honte. — I'm ashamed.

note: l'avenir = the future (what lies ahead); le futur is mostly the grammar tense.
ex: Pense à ton avenir. — Think about your future.

note: As an adjective: stupid, silly (c'est bête = that's silly).

ex: Bonsoir, madame. — Good evening, madam.
Il s'est mis à genoux. — He knelt down.

note: Singular in French: l'escalier = the stairs. escalier roulant = escalator.

ex: Elle avait les larmes aux yeux. — She had tears in her eyes.

note: soir = evening as a point in time; soirée = the evening as a span, or a party.
Takes de before a noun: un million d'euros.

ex: Le lendemain matin, il est parti. — The next morning, he left.
Tu as intérêt à venir. — You'd better come.

note: camarade de classe = classmate.
à droite = on/to the right; but tout droit = straight ahead.
ex: Tournez à droite. — Turn right.

note: faire appel = to appeal (court) or call on.
ex: J'attends ton appel. — I'm waiting for your call.

note: le poste = job/position, (TV/radio) set, police station; la poste = post office, mail.
ex: Il a trouvé un bon poste. — He found a good job.
Je suis en retard. — I'm late.
Tu veux du pain ? — Do you want some bread?
Je l'ai vu par hasard. — I saw him by chance.

note: la mémoire = memory; le mémoire = thesis, report; les mémoires = memoirs.

ex: Les gosses jouent dehors. — The kids are playing outside.

note: Countable: un conseil = a piece of advice, des conseils = advice.
ex: Je peux te donner un conseil ? — Can I give you some advice?

note: Both being with someone (tenir compagnie) and a firm (compagnie aérienne = airline).

ex: Il est en colère. — He is angry.

note: d'occasion = second-hand, used.
ex: J'ai eu l'occasion de le voir. — I had the chance to see him.

faux: on menus = starter, not US main course

note: Also spelled clef. fermer à clé = to lock.
dans la mesure où = insofar as; être en mesure de = to be able to.
coup de fil = phone call; au fil de = over the course of. Plural fils ≠ fils (son).
ex: Passe-moi un coup de fil. — Give me a call.
Répète la phrase. — Repeat the sentence.

faux: any secondary-school teacher, not just a professor
note: Informal: le/la prof.

ex: J'ai sommeil. — I'm sleepy.
Ils habitent à la campagne. — They live in the country.

faux: ≠ glass — ice, ice cream, mirror (glass = verre)
ex: Une glace à la vanille. — A vanilla ice cream.

note: salle de bains = bathroom.
agent (de police) = police officer.
In France: déjeuner = lunch, dîner = evening meal. Also the verb to have dinner.
la page = page (of a book); le page = page boy (rare).
Same spelling as (il) joue = (he) plays.

ex: la moitié du temps — half the time
Je vais faire les courses. — I'm going shopping.

note: Always feminine, even for a man: il a été la victime.
Covers safety too: ceinture de sécurité = seat belt.

ex: Mets des vêtements chauds. — Put on warm clothes.

note: en avance = early; à l'avance / d'avance = in advance.
fer à repasser = (clothes) iron; chemin de fer = railway.
bande dessinée (BD) = comic strip.
Almost always plural: les vacances. Singular la vacance = vacancy (of a post).
ex: On part en vacances. — We're going on holiday.
Quel malheur ! — How awful!

note: Often specifically murder.

ex: un tas de gens — loads of people

note: côte = coast/rib/hill; côté (m) = side. côte à côte = side by side.

ex: un billet de train — a train ticket

note: en arrière = backwards; à l'arrière = in the back.

ex: J'ai rendez-vous chez le médecin. — I have a doctor's appointment.

note: premier étage = first floor above ground (US second floor); ground floor = rez-de-chaussée.

ex: À votre santé ! — Cheers!
Bon courage ! — Good luck! / Hang in there!

note: Capital for people (un Allemand), lowercase for the language (l'allemand).

faux: mainly living room; salon de coiffure = hair salon
also school grade and restaurant bill

note: prendre soin de = to take care of; les soins = (medical) treatment.
ex: Prends soin de toi. — Take care of yourself.

note: tableau (noir) = blackboard.

ex: Quel est ton métier ? — What do you do for a living?
Quel est ton but ? — What's your goal?
en chair et en os — in the flesh
